pages.heading: Chapter 1: Through the Glass
recap: For moons, a pillow cat called Princess Sparkle Muffin watched the wild cats through the glass, while Princess Waffles told the whole story from nineteen floors up.
All day long, Princess Sparkle Muffin had watched the birds through the glass, and nothing ever got past her eyes.
One evening the Tall One opened the door, and Princess Sparkle Muffin chased a moth straight out onto the grass.
The Tall One left the door open a crack, with a dish of water on the warm step.
In the garden, Princess Sparkle Muffin spotted the thirteenth sparrow and said so out loud, and Tallyheart said she had sharp eyes.
In the hidden camp, she told Glintstar, “I want to learn everything.”
Glintstar gave her one moon to show she belonged, and the whole Clan purred her new name: Moonpaw.
Tallyheart taught her the very first Count, the tails, and scratched a claw mark into the leaning tree.
When she worried about being too small, Tallyheart said small cats fit where big cats can’t.
When a great storm crashed down on the river, Tallyheart lay across the doorway, and Moonpaw slept warm in her very own nest.

pages.heading: Chapter 2: After the Storm
recap: The morning after the storm, Tallyheart taught Moonpaw her second Count, the ears, and scratched a second claw mark beside the first.
Then she counted the prey pile, stacked in pairs, and found only sixteen pieces where the old tom’s patrol had stacked twenty.
Moonpaw said so out loud, and her voice rang across the whole camp.
Four pieces of prey were gone, and Glintstar said not one cat had noticed, except the newest.
On her first walk around the territory, three dogs at the Barking Field decided she was a rude squirrel.
At the Crossing, an otter pup named Riffle gave her a lucky stone, and nobody believed her about airplanes.
On the way home, she sneaked under the Old Bridge and saw two big eyes blink in the dark, though snakes can’t blink.
That night, Riffle’s lucky stone lay in Moonpaw’s nest, and she wondered what strange thing was happening on the river.

pages.heading: Chapter 1: Through the Glass
recap: For moons, a pillow cat called Princess Sparkle Muffin watched the wild cats through the glass, while Princess Waffles told the whole story from nineteen floors up.
All day long, Princess Sparkle Muffin had watched the birds through the glass, and nothing ever got past her eyes.
One evening the Tall One opened the door, and Princess Sparkle Muffin chased a moth straight out onto the grass.
The Tall One left the door open a crack, with a dish of water on the warm step.
In the garden, Princess Sparkle Muffin spotted the thirteenth sparrow and said so out loud, and Tallyheart said she had sharp eyes.
In the hidden camp, she told Glintstar, “I want to learn everything.”
Glintstar gave her one moon to show she belonged, and the whole Clan purred her new name: Moonpaw.
Tallyheart taught her the very first Count, the tails, and scratched a claw mark into the leaning tree.
When she worried about being too small, Tallyheart said small cats fit where big cats can’t.
When a great storm crashed down on the river, Tallyheart lay across the doorway, and Moonpaw slept warm in her very own nest.

pages.heading: Chapter 2: After the Storm
recap: The morning after the storm, Tallyheart taught Moonpaw her second Count, the ears, and scratched a second claw mark beside the first.
Then she counted the prey pile, stacked in pairs, and found only sixteen pieces where the old tom’s patrol had stacked twenty.
Moonpaw said so out loud, and her voice rang across the whole camp.
Four pieces of prey were gone, and Glintstar said not one cat had noticed, except the newest.
On her first walk around the territory, three dogs at the Barking Field decided she was a rude squirrel.
At the Crossing, an otter pup named Riffle gave her a lucky stone, and nobody believed her about airplanes.
On the way home, she sneaked under the Old Bridge and saw two big eyes blink in the dark, though snakes can’t blink.
That night, Riffle’s lucky stone lay in Moonpaw’s nest, and she wondered what strange thing was happening on the river.

pages.heading: Chapter 1: Through the Glass
recap: For moons, a pillow cat called Princess Sparkle Muffin watched the wild cats through the glass, while Princess Waffles told the whole story from nineteen floors up.
All day long, Princess Sparkle Muffin had ambushed socks from the laundry basket, and no sock in the building was safe.
One evening the Tall One opened the door, and Princess Sparkle Muffin stepped out slowly, one paw at a time, onto the grass.
The Tall One left the door open a crack, with a dish of water on the warm step.
In the garden, Princess Sparkle Muffin kept quiet about the thirteenth sparrow, but Tallyheart sniffed her out anyway and said she had sharp eyes.
In the hidden camp, she told Glintstar, “I can learn to count anything.”
Glintstar gave her one moon to show she belonged, and the whole Clan purred her new name: Moonpaw.
Tallyheart taught her the very first Count, the tails, and scratched a claw mark into the leaning tree.
When she worried about the deep river, Tallyheart promised they would take it one paw at a time.
When a great storm crashed down on the river, Tallyheart lay across the doorway, and Moonpaw slept warm in her very own nest.

pages.heading: Chapter 2: After the Storm
recap: The morning after the storm, Tallyheart taught Moonpaw her second Count, the ears, and scratched a second claw mark beside the first.
Then she counted the prey pile, stacked in pairs, and found only sixteen pieces where the old tom’s patrol had stacked twenty.
Moonpaw whispered it to Tallyheart, and Tallyheart told the whole camp who had noticed.
Four pieces of prey were gone, and Glintstar said not one cat had noticed, except the newest.
On her first walk around the territory, three dogs at the Barking Field decided she was a rude squirrel.
At the Crossing, an otter pup named Riffle gave her a lucky stone, and nobody believed her about airplanes.
On the way home, she heard something on the tallest tower roar back at an airplane, with a tiny hiccup at the end.
That night, Riffle’s lucky stone lay in Moonpaw’s nest, and she wondered what strange thing was happening on the river.
